channel.description: An unfiltered record of rebuilding a life, a mind, and a creative spark after a year of compounding losses.

item.title: Blind Amnesia
item.description: The more time that passes, the more the good gets highlighted, and the bad fades into nothingness.
item.content:encoded:
I’m missing my ex today. It’s been almost exactly 2 months, and I guess things hit harder on milestones. The more time that passes, the more the good gets highlighted, and the bad fades into nothingness.

It was my choice to walk away. Our arguments were becoming more frequent, and instead of seeing growth in how we resolved things, I saw decline. I became increasingly frustrated at how long it took for the smallest issues to get resolved. It was in that frustration that I began to realise I was becoming someone I did not want to be.

Dealing with the passing of my dad had a big effect on it all. I was letting myself go. I stopped exercise and I wasn’t eating much. But I couldn’t manage to pull myself together because every time I found the smallest amount of motivation or happiness an argument would erupt and pull me back down.

I knew that I had to walk away, but I still loved her. It’s a cruel thing, love, in many ways. How we love what is not good for us. How we spend so much time hoping that things will improve despite all evidence to the contrary.

I finally found the courage to leave. And life did get better. For me, it almost always does after a breakup. I tend to use the time to focus inward, to find myself again, and to return to who I am. And that’s exactly what happened this time. I got back to being me.

Without the regular arguments, my free time was filled with peace and silence. All year I had needed that, and finally it was here. There was now a space for me to feel and to begin truly healing the wounds that my dad’s passing had left behind.

Still, I long for the good times. The happiness in imagining a future together. The warm cuddles and comforting laughs. No relationship is all bad, and walking away leaves you missing what had been good all along.

I catch myself in moments as I notice the blind amnesia. The focus on only what was good. I forget that I had lost myself; I forget that I had been lacking the room to breathe, and I forget that I was not able to show up authentically in my grief.

I’m having one of those moments right now as I write this. Looking back on old photos, following old chains of thought. Questioning my decisions. There is a sadness, but behind it, logic still rules. I did what was best for me. At least for now.

item.title: The Sting of Silence
item.description: A reflection on the pros and cons of the now traditional dopamine hits provided by online platforms.
item.content:encoded:
Since putting my writing back online I have noticed an odd silence. This site is static, and it has no integrated feedback loop. It has made me realise that I have grown accustomed to the reactions and comments provided by modern platforms.

Identifying a Conflict

My workflow has been to create, then upload, then obsessively check the reactions. And if my art performed poorly, it would affect my emotional state. Making me want to quit, or worse still, hide away.

Publishing something here leaves me with no feedback, no little hearts of recognition, no comments to satisfy or destroy my ego. Just silence. The act of posting completes the work of creation.

Its oddly satisfying, almost like sitting alone at the beach listening to the waves roll in. Or rolling up the tent door from a mountain top to witness the birds dancing at sunrise.

Attention Cravings

Even so part of me craves that feedback loop. I want to know if people are seeing me. I want to know what they think about what I have to say. I find the option of accepting feedback practical. It helps to improve and to motivate.

Although, if I am being honest, those wants also assume that feedback is positive.

Silent Relief

A different part of me finds relief in the silence. The opinions of others have no control over the value I place on my art. I can create freely. I can love the process, and I can love the results. Then I can release it, no feedback, no outside influence to affect my emotional stability. Only my opinion and my happiness for having created something.

I find posting into silence romantic and freeing. It lets me create as if in private while still sharing a piece of me with an unknown and possibly non-existent audience. Instead of holding the work open for reaction, it marks the end of the creation process. The posting becomes an act of release.

So What Now

As I write this, I am trying to decide which of these two paths will serve me better long term. Should I implement reactions and comments or should I embrace the silence?

I don’t have the answer today. So for now I will do nothing and continue to relish the space that comes after hitting upload.

item.title: Running Toward the Light
item.description: A raw look at how I'm turning the hardest year of my life into a reason to keep pushing forward.
item.content:encoded:
The Weight of it All

First, let me fill you in on the current situation.

I’m based in Valencia, Spain. Recently single, going through the hardest year of my life.

Its not only that my relationship ended, or that I got caught up being an unexpected dad to 5 guinea pigs.

Its not only that I lost my dad right before New Years, or that the funeral preparations were an absolute disaster full of opportunists, or that the circumstances around his death were extremely suspicious.

Its not only that my sister decided to stop speaking to me during all of this, or that I stopped eating and lost 10kg of muscle.

Its not only that my one best friend left the city, or that my savings are running low, or that AI has shaken up my career landscape.

But the worst of it all is that I lost my confidence and my own mind turned against me. For a while anyway.

Putting Up a Fight

The more life beat me, the less effect it seemed to have. I began to realise that at the end of all of this I too would end up taking the long cold nap and nothing that happened today was really as serious as that.

And my dad always told me:

“Never give up”

So I summoned what was left inside of me and started to dig my way back out.

Hitting the Pavement

I got back into running and found a release from the stress.

I often hoped a day would come that I would spend mornings running on the beach with my dad. That day never came. Yet despite him being gone I feel him running with me now, even though he hated running.

In the last 18 weeks I went from the couch to my first half marathon. And now I’ve started training for my first full one. I’m at 26 of 42 km so far.

Sunrises and Sea Water

I’ve also been running a community with some friends that meets every Tuesday to watch the sunrise from the ocean water.

I can’t say its been easy, many Tuesday mornings I wished I could avoid it. But I’m happy I didn’t, it’s kept me at least a little sane through this absolute ringer of a year.

Connecting with Something Greater

I found God again, or perhaps God found me. Not in the traditional religious sense. I don’t find myself aligning with Christianity, or Catholicism, or Islam. I just feel connected with this idea that there is something greater and grander than what we are. Something that many call God, but then go on to define in different ways.

I’ve been talking to Him. Very relaxed like, as if speaking with an old friend, and it’s been helping me. I also talk to my dad. Both are one way conversations.

Building an Escape Hatch

I’ve been putting in work to grow on social media, rather unsuccessfully I might add. Most days I consider quitting, but then I remind myself of the internal growth that showing up has given me.

Facing the embarrassment of failing in public, and accepting the sting of working on something you are proud of. Only for it to receive no recognition.

Its been a whirlwind of an adventure. From not caring, to caring, to caring too much, to realising its only ever been about creating to being with.

One Step in Front of the Other

For the most part, life is a mixture of hope and fear. Hope, for the positive change that I can see in the light at the end of this tunnel. Fear, for the possibility that I am wrong about that light and it just turns out to be more darkness.

Regardless I carry on daily. Because I have come to realise that when you don’t know what to do just put one foot in front of the other and hope that your legs take you to a better place.

The Path Forward

During this process I stumbled across my old writings. Blogs, short stories, and poems. All outlets that I used to value once upon a time.

After reading and feeling the past through them I’ve decided to return to the world of pen to paper, or finger to key. And as testimony to that, this is my first addition to my new collection of writings. Because even if nobody ever reads this, I may stumble across it in the future and remember what it was like to be here today.

And be thankful that I made it through it all.
